summary: The 2026-10-20 public knowledge receiver matrix preserved its failed phases and already-passed subjects instead of replacing evidence with a clean rerun. In the retained nonempty Standard-to-FSharp receiver, the actual migration succeeded before the fixture rejected migration-unexpected-output: SDD authority locking legitimately leaves .fsgg/typed-sdd-transactions/authority.lock as a zero-byte file. The corrected adapter admits that exact empty regular, non-symlink file alongside six expected new paths; foreign outputs and nonempty locks remain refusals. The documented recovery bound the already-applied receiver, original journal/checkpoint digests and saved subject bytes/modes. It retained the expired operation and its deadline, then used a separately admitted, explicitly identified operation with its own absolute bound including validation and cleanup. A new clock did not renew the expired operation or authorize replay. Recovery performed only the remaining knowledge and rollback assertions: it did not recreate the receiver, repeat migration/apply, or rerun the 21 previously passed subjects. Required knowledge-probe and Git-bundle scratch clones remain valid remaining assertions; distinguish a retained receiver used as clone source from a newly created receiver destination. Rollback restored owner Standard/product/tool/guide/CI bytes and modes while preserving canonical knowledge records and history. The report establishes 22 supported passes and two producer-held Python Wizard positives, not acceptance of all 24 rows. A compatible published supplier and the two actual remaining assertions are still required for that full matrix; separately deferred bindings positives remain outside its denominator. Source delivery, required CI, publication/adoption, parent acceptance and present operational authorization remain distinct. The adapter cited at the report revision is byte-identical to the executed adapter revision; these citations preserve a scoped historical finding, not permission for another operation.
title: Public receiver recovery preserves failed evidence, expired clocks and acceptance scope
